items.stem: Which term matches this definition: “evaluation of a study by independent experts before publication”?
items.markingKey: Peer review: evaluation of a study by independent experts before publication. [1]

items.stem: Explain why a research proposal on the under-representation of women in parliaments should include a section headed “Methods and sources”.
items.answer: It shows how the question will be answered and whether the evidence needed is accessible.

items.stem: “The voting age should be lowered to 16.” To what extent do you agree with this statement?
items.answer: For: 16-year-olds will live longest with the results of today’s decisions. People who vote in their first election are more likely to keep voting. After Austria lowered the voting age to 16 in 2007, studies found that 16- and 17-year-olds turned out at rates similar to slightly older first-time voters. Against: 16-year-olds are easily influenced by parents and teachers. The argument assumes that 16-year-olds are mature enough to make informed voting decisions. Judgement: A sustained answer weighs the evidence and reaches a qualified judgement (response to objection: research finds young voters’ choices are no less consistent with their own views than older voters’).
items.markingKey: Level 1 (1–2 marks): simple, one-sided assertions with little support. Level 2 (3–4 marks): explains arguments on one side well, or both sides in less depth, using some evidence or examples. Level 3 (5–6 marks): balanced analysis of different perspectives, evidence evaluated for quality, and a reasoned, supported judgement on “to what extent”. [6]

items.stem: Which ethical principle requires that participants’ names and identifying details are not included in the report?
items.markingKey: Anonymity: participants’ names and identifying details are not included in the report. [1]

items.stem: A report’s conclusion reads: “In conclusion, this report has proved conclusively that economic sanctions are rarely an effective way to change a government’s behaviour; no reasonable person could disagree.” What is the main weakness?
options: It introduces new evidence in the conclusion
It contradicts the analysis in the report
It does not answer the question

items.stem: To what extent do you agree that student primary research adds little of value to a report on the use of economic sanctions compared with published research? Consider different perspectives in your answer.
items.answer: For: Student samples are small and unrepresentative. Published research uses larger samples and peer-reviewed methods. Against: Primary research can explore a local context or perspective that published research ignores. Triangulating local data with published studies can reveal differences. Judgement: Primary research is most valuable when clearly limited in its claims and used alongside published evidence.

items.stem: Explain two reasons why a student researching state use of facial recognition surveillance should keep a detailed research log.
items.answer: It records decisions and reasons as they happen, so changes of direction can be explained and justified; it provides evidence for honest reflection on methods, problems and learning; it shows the work is the student’s own.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each reason, 1 mark each developed [2]

items.stem: Evaluate the view that ethical rules make it too difficult for students to research sensitive political issues such as the under-representation of women in parliaments.
items.answer: For: Consent and anonymity requirements limit who can be interviewed. Some groups (refugees, officials) may be inaccessible or vulnerable. Against: Secondary sources and anonymised surveys still allow rigorous research. Ethical rules protect participants and make findings more trustworthy. Judgement: Ethics shape the methods rather than preventing research; good design can meet both aims.

items.markingKey: Confidentiality: information given by participants is stored securely and not shared beyond the research. [1]

items.stem: In a research report on low voter turnout among young people, which sentence is written in the most appropriate academic style?
options: Everyone knows the policy obviously worked.
This evidence suggests that the policy may have increased turnout among some groups.
This totally proves the policy was brilliant.
I reckon the policy worked loads.
items.answer: This evidence suggests that the policy may have increased turnout among some groups.
items.markingKey: Formal register, hedged claim, no colloquial or absolute language. [1]

items.stem: “Grey literature from NGOs and governments is as valuable as academic research for a report on low voter turnout among young people.” To what extent do you agree with this statement?
items.answer: For: NGO and government reports are often more current and contain field data. They reveal the perspectives of key stakeholders. Against: They are not peer reviewed and may reflect vested interests. Academic research uses transparent methods and engages with theory. Judgement: Grey literature is valuable for perspectives and recent data, but must be evaluated and corroborated against academic research.

items.stem: A student uses a report by an independent election-monitoring mission as evidence in a report on the under-representation of women in parliaments. Evaluate its credibility.
items.answer: Strength: its observers were present at polling stations and are trained to assess elections. Weakness: observers can visit only a sample of polling stations. It should be corroborated by independent evidence.
items.markingKey: 1 mark strength; 1 mark weakness; 1 mark corroboration or judgement [2]

items.stem: To what extent do you agree that in a research report on lowering the voting age to 16, academic style matters as much as content? Consider different perspectives in your answer.
items.answer: For: Precise, hedged language shows the strength of evidence accurately. Consistent referencing makes the research checkable and credible. Against: A well-styled report with weak analysis remains weak. Assessment rewards analysis, evaluation and judgement most. Judgement: Style serves content: it cannot replace strong analysis, but poor style can undermine it.

items.stem: A report on lowering the voting age to 16 includes evidence from a political scientist who has studied Austria (reports that 16- and 17-year-olds there turned out at rates similar to young adults) and from a student union (supports voting at 16). Explain how the student could synthesise these perspectives rather than simply describe them.
items.answer: Identify where they agree and disagree, explain why (e.g. she bases her view on election data; its members are directly affected), weigh the quality of the evidence each uses, and combine insights into a judgement on the question.
items.markingKey: 1 mark agreement/disagreement; 1 mark explains differences; 1 mark weighs evidence; 1 mark combined judgement [2]

items.stem: Grace argues that feasibility should be the most important factor when choosing a research report topic. How far do you agree? Support your answer with reasoning and evidence.
items.answer: For: A topic without accessible evidence cannot be researched properly. Time and word limits are fixed. Against: Without interest, motivation fades over a long project. A topic needs a genuine academic debate and alternative perspectives. Judgement: Feasibility is a necessary condition, but the best topics, e.g. on migration caused by climate change, combine interest, debate and access to evidence.
